The Inventory Management System (IMS), formerly referred to as the Terminal Tracking Application, is a purpose-built standalone web application for Terminal Distributor — a global payment terminal distributor managing serialised payment devices across a worldwide warehouse network. The application serves as the master system of record for terminal serial number states, inventory counts, order management, and cost tracking.

Release 1 is complete and running locally. This document captures the v1.2 updates: a set of R1 patch items identified post-build (UI improvements and label corrections), and the full R2 feature scope including inventory enhancements, cost calculation engine, cost analytics, and all previously planned planning and integration modules.
Technology stack: React + Vite frontend with e2open teal green (#1A6B7B) navbar, Python
backend, SQLite (local) upgradeable to PostgreSQL, Tailwind CSS.

9.2 In Transit View — Full Transit State Coverage
The In Transit view (R1 Patch: formerly 'Expecting') is expanded to display all terminals currently in any of the following states:
EXPECTING — terminal serial declared by supplier; PO shipment not yet received at warehouse
TRANSIT_TO_COMPANY — terminal shipped outbound to customer on a Sales, Replacement, or Rental order

The In Transit view displays the following columns for all state types: Serial Number, Product Code, Current State, Origin Location, Destination Location, Carrier, Carrier Tracking Reference, Estimated Arrival Date (ETA), Order/PO Reference, and Latest Date.
This provides a unified 'in movement' dashboard for Supply Planners monitoring all terminals currently not at a fixed location.

The Cost Calculation Engine automatically computes and maintains the accumulated cost per terminal serial number based on activity costs incurred at each state transition.
When a terminal transitions from one state to another, the system:

Looks up the Activity Cost Master for a matching record: Location (current) + State (new state entered) + Product Code (optional override). If a product-specific cost exists, it takes priority over the generic
Identifies the cost amount and currency from the matched record.
Identifies the reporting currency of the current location from the Location Master.
Applies the Exchange Rate Master to convert the activity cost from its native currency to the location's reporting currency, using the exchange rate effective on the date of the state transition.
Adds the converted cost amount to the serial number's

The state history record for this transition stores the raw activity cost amount, native currency, reporting currency equivalent, and exchange rate applied — providing a full cost audit trail per transition.
If no matching Activity Cost Master record exists for a given location + state combination, the system records the transition with zero cost for that activity and logs a warning for Admin review.
For IN_REPAIR state transitions, the standard Activity Cost Master value is used as an estimate. When the Repair Centre user completes the repair and enters the actual cost, the system:
Records the actual cost (amount + currency) on the Repair Order record.
Calculates the difference between the actual cost and the standard estimate already applied to the accumulated cost.
Records the adjustment in the state history cost audit trail with a note indicating it is an actual-cost correction.

The accumulated cost is displayed on the Terminal Detail view with a cost breakdown table showing each contributing state transition: state entered, date, location, activity cost (native currency), exchange rate applied, and reporting currency equivalent. The total is shown at the bottom in the location's reporting currency.
